messages:
sylvia: heads-up — provisioning wave in eu-west4 stalled, lots of PROVISIONING_HOLDs. I traced to a weird NVMe "swapback" behaviour on a small cohort (scratch-44). Hosts showing IO stalls when the controller transitions power states.
noah: expand "swapback"?
infra-bot: [ALERT] scratch-44-node[2-5]: nvme_pm_state_change events 8 -> 23 in last 20m; p99 write_latency 750ms -> 3.6s; media_errors +2 each.
sylvia: kernel logs show controller PM transitions interleaving with janitor deep-scrub fsyncs — leads to a burst of smallwrites queued and a short period where the controller stalls while switching PM states. dmesg snippet: 
```
[1789123432.001] nvme0: PM state change: 3->1
[1789123432.004] nvme0: I/O timeout, cmd 0x27
[1789123433.112] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
```
ram: oh nice catch. That's different from plain wear or badblocks. Might be firmware PM aggressiveness + scrub churn. Any scrub concurrency spikes?
kate: janitor metrics show scratch-44 had concurrency=18 for a forced reclaim test; scrub_started 1789123400. Provisioner surge ~1789123420. Bad overlap.
sylvia: immediate mitigation plan proposed: 1) reduce janitor concurrency to 2 for cohort scratch-44, 2) label nodes to stop new attaches, 3) set provisioner backoff, 4) run smartctl short and schedule long test on flagged hosts.
noah: please patch config and label. Also create a short-lived cron that auto-labels nodes if PM state changes >5 in 15m.
sylvia: patching now: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_workers":"2","cohort_overrides":"scratch-44:2"}}'
kubectl label nodes -l cohort=scratch-44 no-new-gpu-attach=true
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/provisioner ATTACH_BACKOFF_MS=45000
```
infra-bot: [INFO] patch applied by sylvia at 1789123440. janitor max_workers=2 for scratch-44; nodes labeled.
ram: quick iostat 90s after patch: 
```
Device            r/s    w/s   await
nvme0n1          0.04   88.00   2.0
nvme1n1          0.01   22.00   0.8
```
ram: attach success rate jumped from ~79% -> 97% in the last 7m. Queue drained.
kate: smartctl short from node scratch-44-node3: 
```
SMART overall-health: PASSED
Media Errors: 1
Temperature: 48 C
```
noah: good sign but we should still run long test and capture firmware PM logs. I'll open INFRA-6001 to track firmware PM telemetry ingestion and cohort guardrails.
sylvia: cost ops — if we shift urgent onboards to eu-west2 fallback for 1h what's the rough hit? We want to avoid large cross-region moves unless critical.
oncall-sre: quick estimate ~ $310 for urgent lanes for 1h (reservation bump + egress). Approve for critical lanes only.
ram: add to INFRA-6001: 1) ingest nvme pm_state_change events into TSDB, 2) create janitor blackout windows during heavy provisioning windows, 3) auto-label nodes on PM event spikes, 4) firmware vendor follow-up for PM aggressiveness.
noah: also add a small tweak: janitor should defer deep-scrub if any node in cohort reports pm_state_change > threshold in last 30m. That avoids repeated flip-flop.
sylvia: agreed. I'll schedule a retro with Janitor, Provisioner, and Firmware teams to decide a sustainable concurrency default and add the blackout scheduler.
kate: rolling a 5m cronjob to auto-label nodes where infra-bot reports pm_state_change > 5 in 15m. Will monitor and remove after ticketed changes.
sylvia: monitoring pinned. I'll follow up after SMART long tests and firmware logs are collected. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
